status: 5 main and 21 supplementary manuscript figures. Prior presentation remains unchanged.

figures.title: Clinical target framework and parallel research EASI estimation
figures.caption: a, Framework development described in the investigator materials: candidate clinical measures, a two-round questionnaire and discussion procedure, 49 returned questionnaires, and a planned agreement criterion of at least 75%. Original ballots and round-specific agreement were unavailable; these are source-reported development details, not independently verified consensus results. b, Scheduled targets transcribed from the project framework. Within each domain, any listed criterion is sufficient; from W4 onward both domains must be met. W2 assesses only PP-NRS ≤4. EASI50 and EASI75 denote at least 50% and 75% improvement from a positive observed baseline EASI. IGA decrease ≥2 is relative to baseline; IGA 0/1 and PP-NRS 0/1 denote observed values 0 or 1. DLQI targets apply to adults aged ≥18 years. Missing components are handled with three-valued logic, rather than automatically classified as target failure. The exact IGA instrument and approved implemented framework version require investigator confirmation. Visits are schematic and not spaced in proportion to time. c, Clinician-directed assessment and care are separated from the research estimator using BSA, CCL17, CCL26 and IL-5. The estimator was not a dose-change rule, and this observational analysis does not establish the effectiveness of the proposed integrated management strategy.

figures.title: Observed clinical activity and target attainment by initial treatment
figures.caption: a–c, Unadjusted observed medians and interquartile ranges for EASI, PP-NRS and adult DLQI at W0, W12 and W24. The observations available at each visit are used; these are not fixed-patient trajectories. d–n, Observed attainment of every specified clinical threshold. Lines join available-case proportions; bands are pointwise Wilson 95% confidence intervals. EASI50/75/90 and IGA decrease ≥2 require a recorded baseline and follow-up; absolute thresholds also show W0. PP-NRS ≤4 additionally includes W2. Adult DLQI uses patients aged ≥18 years. o, Combined physician-and-patient targets from Fig. 1, with Wilson intervals. The combined criteria change by stage, so these points are not connected. Colour identifies initial treatment; later treatment changes do not reassign groups. All achieved/evaluable counts, additional designated visits and missing-outcome bounds are retained in source tables; baseline-adjusted target comparisons are shown in the supplement. Changing available-case denominators and baseline treatment differences preclude a causal comparison. No outcomes are imputed.

figures.title: Recorded skin severity and treatment-reduction pathways
figures.caption: a–c, Recorded IGA compositions at W0, W4, W12 and W24. Each bar totals 100% of the evaluable patients; n below the bar is its patient denominator. The ordered blue scale identifies recorded IGA grades 0–5 and is not a treatment colour. No score or count is superimposed on the segments. All grade-specific counts and proportions remain in source tables. d–f, Future-defined pathways formed by W12 EASI75 status and subsequent recorded treatment changes. Horizontal bar length is the proportion of the complete initial group (N=65/56/42), and the number at its end is the pathway size. The seven mutually exclusive rows exhaust each initial group, including zero-size and uncertain-exposure rows. Reached refers to W12 EASI75; later reduction means a documented reduction after W12. These are descriptive pathways, not randomized reduction strategies; the bars do not encode subsequent efficacy or relapse. Instrument identity remains unverified for the recorded IGA scale. Complete pathway counts are available in source data.

figures.title: Serum molecular response during the first 12 weeks
figures.caption: a–c, Mean within-patient change in log₂ concentration from W0 to W12 and 95% t confidence intervals for all 23 markers, by initial treatment. A change of −1 corresponds to half the baseline concentration. d–e, Direct adjusted differences in those changes for A200 minus A100 and dupilumab minus pooled abrocitinib, with HC3-robust 95% confidence intervals. Models adjust for starting log₂ concentration, W0 EASI, age, sex, BMI and centre. Pooled abrocitinib preserves the observed dose mixture. Negative contrasts mean a larger decline in the first group. Stars show q<0.05 under the original declared BH families; no tests or multiplicity families were changed for this display. Each marker uses its own available pairs. Estimates with fewer than five pairs have no inferential interval or star; missing estimates are left blank. Exact sample sizes, estimates, intervals and q values remain in source tables. Within-group and between-group panels have separately labelled x axes and cannot be interpreted as the same effect. The remaining pairwise treatment contrasts, later windows, fixed three-visit trajectories and assay-batch sensitivities are reported in the supplement. Treatment assignment was observational.

figures.title: Individual EASI estimation error and EASI75 response classification
figures.caption: a, Cumulative absolute-error proportions for the common BSA–CCL17–CCL26–IL-5 procedure. Each repetition is scored before averaging; bands are patient-bootstrap 95% confidence intervals conditional on saved predictions. All predictions enter the proportions, although thresholds are displayed only through ten points. The two-point line is a reading reference, not an accepted replacement margin. W0/W12/W24 include 152/89/75 patients. b, EASI75 sensitivity, specificity and agreement with observed response, with patient-bootstrap 95% confidence intervals. Each response uses its corresponding observed or estimated W0 and follow-up score. W12/W24 sensitivity denominators are 49/54 observed responders; specificity denominators are 36/13 nonresponders; agreement includes 85/67 patients. W0/W12 use nested patient-level validation; W24 is previously inspected same-cohort temporal application. Metrics assess the development procedure, not independent validation of the final formula. Numerical metrics and matched controls are in Table 2; additional agreement and paired-change analyses are in the supplement.

figures.title: Patient and record flow into the clinical and model analyses
figures.caption: a, The curated clinical source contains 170 patients, not a screened or consented recruitment denominator. Six patients aged <12 years and one age-eligible patient with an ambiguous initial dose are excluded, leaving 163 patients classified by initial treatment: dupilumab, 65; abrocitinib 100 mg, 56; and abrocitinib 200 mg, 42. b, The linked serum source is a separate entry branch; model eligibility is not conditional on membership of the clinical comparison population. Removing 24 W48 records leaves 168 patients with 352 W0/W12/W24 records; age exclusions remove 12 records from six patients. Further ordered exclusions are mutually exclusive at the record level: 13 EASI, one BSA, zero CCL17, eight CCL26 and two IL-5 inputs are unavailable, leaving 316 complete model visits from 160 patients. A valid molecular input requires an available positive concentration for the log2 transformation. Loss of a record does not necessarily remove a patient. Development uses 241 W0/W12 visits from 156 patients, with patient-level validation splits; W24 includes 75 visits from 75 patients and is previously inspected within-cohort temporal application, not external validation. Development and W24 share 71 patients, with 85 development-only and four W24-only patients. Fifty-one patients have all three complete visits. The clinical and complete-input model populations share 159 patients, with four clinical-only and one model-only patient; the treatment-free model can retain an ambiguous initial dose. Scheduled empty visit slots are not counted as observed visits, and no filled-in clinical outcome is used as validation truth.

figures.title: Baseline balance, treatment overlap and effective sample size
figures.caption: a–c, Absolute standardized mean differences for every covariate in the initial-treatment propensity model, before and after generalized overlap weighting. Differences use the unweighted pairwise pooled standard deviation in both displays. The light 0.10 reference line is a descriptive balance guide, not a statistical significance threshold. Residual imbalance remains. d–f, Baseline multinomial treatment probabilities, stratified by actual initial treatment; each distribution uses all patients in that initial group and sums to 100%. These show common support rather than longitudinal drug exposure. The footer reports original N and effective sample size, (sum w)²/sum(w²). All centre, sex, age, BMI and EASI variables are shown. Overlap weighting targets comparable baseline patients; it cannot remove unmeasured confounding or correct outcome-driven dose changes. Endpoint- and marker-specific availability/ESS diagnostics are retained in the source tables.

figures.title: Observed and adjusted BSA (%), SCORAD
figures.caption: Left, observed medians with interquartile ranges by initial treatment; all available values are used at each specified visit. Right, generalized-overlap-weighted marginal estimates with patient-cluster robust 95% confidence intervals, adjusted for baseline outcome, age, sex, BMI and centre. Patient sets can differ between visits. Exact outcome-specific counts and numerical comparisons are in the source tables; they are not replaced by a common denominator. Initial treatment groups describe observational management strategies, including subsequent regimen changes, rather than randomized fixed-dose effects.

figures.title: Observed and adjusted IgE (recorded units), Eosinophils (recorded units)
figures.caption: Left, observed medians with interquartile ranges by initial treatment; all available values are used at each specified visit. Right, generalized-overlap-weighted marginal estimates with patient-cluster robust 95% confidence intervals, adjusted for baseline outcome, age, sex, BMI and centre. Patient sets can differ between visits. Exact outcome-specific counts and numerical comparisons are in the source tables; they are not replaced by a common denominator. IgE and eosinophils use log(1+x) models and back-transformation; adjusted estimates are not arithmetic means. IgE is shown only at W0/W12/W24. No dupilumab W4 eosinophil measurement is available; both the observed and adjusted line break at that visit. No multiple-imputation value is displayed as an observation. The separate same-patient IgE analysis tests the effect of changing sample composition. Initial treatment groups describe observational management strategies, including subsequent regimen changes, rather than randomized fixed-dose effects.

figures.title: IgE with identical patients at W0, W12 and W24
figures.caption: Medians and patient-bootstrap 95% confidence intervals in fixed complete three-visit sets: 11 dupilumab, 9 A100 and 10 A200 patients. The same patients contribute at every visit within each treatment. The vertical axis is logarithmic with ticks labelled in the original recorded units; estimates and interval endpoints are unchanged. Small horizontal offsets separate treatment intervals at the same visit. No missing value is filled. These fixed-set summaries differ from available-case visit summaries and baseline-adjusted estimates because their patients and estimands differ. This check describes observation-pattern sensitivity: the small selected subsets neither estimate a causal treatment effect nor establish arithmetic mean changes. Laboratory units require source confirmation.

figures.title: Week 2: all initial-treatment target contrasts
figures.caption: Observed and baseline-adjusted risk differences with nominal 95% confidence intervals. Positive values favour the first named treatment for target attainment. Adjustment uses generalized overlap weights from baseline EASI, age, sex, BMI and centre; it does not estimate a randomized current-dose effect. D denotes dupilumab; A100/A200 the initial abrocitinib doses. Pooled abrocitinib is supplementary. Missing estimates are left absent; all exact denominators, Fisher/weighted tests, Holm-adjusted P values and exploratory FDR values are in the source tables.

figures.title: Baseline distributions of all 23 serum markers
figures.caption: Cells display the lower quartile, median and upper quartile of baseline log₂ recorded concentration for each initial treatment. All three panels use the same numeric colour scale without row normalization. Compare treatments within a marker: concentration differences between distinct analytes do not indicate differences in biological activity. D denotes dupilumab; A100/A200 initial abrocitinib 100/200 mg. Every measured marker is retained. The source table includes exact counts, censoring-related availability, ranges and distribution summaries; quartiles summarize available positive numeric observations and do not replace censored values.

figures.title: Molecular changes from W12 to W24
figures.caption: Mean paired log₂ concentration changes with 95% t confidence intervals. Negative values indicate lower later concentration. Each marker/treatment uses all available pairs for this interval; exact counts are in the source table. All 23 measured markers are retained. Estimates based on fewer than five pairs are descriptive and have no inferential interval; unavailable estimates are blank. Stars denote BH q<0.05 across the full 207 marker-by-treatment-by-window family, not a separate family for the displayed interval.

figures.title: Adjusted molecular comparisons from W0 to W12
figures.caption: Differences in within-patient log₂ changes with HC3 95% confidence intervals. Negative values mean a smaller, more negative change in the first named treatment. Models adjust starting log₂ concentration, baseline total EASI, age, sex, BMI and centre. D, dupilumab; A100/A200, initial abrocitinib 100/200 mg. Pooled A retains the observed dose mixture. Stars denote the original BH q<0.05 family; no multiplicity family is recalculated after display selection. Blank positions have no estimable contrast. Complete counts, diagnostics, centre/batch sensitivities and tests remain in the source table. The W0–W12 D-minus-pooled-A and A200-minus-A100 comparisons are in the main molecular figure. These are adjusted observational associations, not randomized current-dose effects.

figures.title: Molecular and clinical changes associated after multiplicity correction
figures.caption: Every association meeting BH q<0.05 in the full declared change-association family is displayed; selection spans 23 markers, five clinical outcomes, three initial treatments and three intervals. No W12–W24 association met this threshold. Points are Spearman correlations between within-patient clinical change and log₂ molecular change, both later minus earlier, with patient-bootstrap 95% confidence intervals. Positive correlations indicate changes in the same direction. Labels give paired-patient counts and the interval; colours indicate initial treatment only. Adult DLQI requires age ≥18. All tested coefficients, non-significant results and unestimable pairs remain in the complete source table. This significance-selected display is exploratory and is not independent validation, numerical agreement or a causal molecular effect.

figures.title: Regional clinical burden and molecular associations
figures.caption: a, Baseline Spearman associations between all 23 markers and the four regional EASI contributions; stars mark BH q<0.05, with complete coefficients, patient counts and bootstrap intervals retained in the source. b, Available-case mean regional EASI divided by its theoretical maximum and multiplied by 100; cells show percentages, not patient counts. c, Mean paired regional decrease as a percentage of the same regional maximum for three separately labelled intervals; positive values indicate improvement. D is dupilumab and A is the observed pooled abrocitinib dose mixture. These heatmaps summarize magnitude; exact 95% t intervals and counts are in the source tables. d, Whole-body PP-NRS mean decreases with 95% t intervals, not region-specific itch. Regional maxima are 7.2, 14.4, 21.6 and 28.8 for head/neck, upper limbs, trunk and lower limbs. All regional analyses require complete, bounded regional records consistent with total EASI. Intervals can share patients and are not successive cumulative effects. Colour bars encode distinct quantities and are not interchangeable. No baseline-adjusted regional treatment contrast passed the FDR threshold; full separate-dose comparisons remain available.

figures.title: Three-visit molecular trajectories in fixed patient sets
figures.caption: Within each marker and treatment, the same patients contribute at W0, W12 and W24. W0 is zero by definition; W12/W24 are mean within-patient log₂ changes from W0. Light blue, teal and deep blue encode W0/W12/W24 consistently across all panels. Rows are spaced to separate the three visits; horizontal intervals are 95% t confidence intervals for n≥5. Smaller sets are descriptive without inferential intervals, and absent estimates remain blank. All 23 markers are retained. Fixed triplet counts are available in the source table and may differ across markers or treatments, but never across the three displayed visits within a marker/treatment.

figures.title: Observed and estimated EASI at each visit
figures.caption: a–c, Estimated versus observed EASI in the first patient-held-out repetition at W0/W12 and same-cohort temporal application at W24. Each fixed 2×2-EASI-point cell counts all exact score pairs within its boundaries. Colour gives patient count on one shared logarithmic scale; white cells contain no observations. All 152/89/75 eligible patients are retained. Identical axes preserve the severity-range comparison; grey diagonals denote exact agreement. W0/W12 use nested patient-level structure and penalty selection; earlier marker selection is not repeated. W24 had previously been inspected. These results assess the development procedure rather than independent validation of the final coefficient vector. Overall performance is in Table 2; the main figure displays the complete absolute-error distribution.

figures.title: Within-patient EASI change and absolute error
figures.caption: a–c, Estimated versus observed EASI changes in the first patient-held-out repetition. Change is end minus start: negative values indicate improvement. Fixed 2×2-EASI-point cells count exact paired changes on one logarithmic count scale. Identical axes retain all 85, 67 and 55 pairs; the intervals can share patients and are not consecutive categories on a time axis. White cells contain no observations; diagonals mark exact agreement. d, Change MAE calculated within each of two repetitions before averaging, with 2,000 patient-bootstrap 95% confidence intervals conditional on saved predictions. Both scores are paired within each repetition before subtraction. W24 is previously inspected same-cohort temporal application. EASI75 classification is shown in the main model figure; complete EASI50/75/90 classifications are retained separately.

figures.title: Classification of EASI50, EASI75 and EASI90 response
figures.caption: Each panel shows actual patient counts from the first outer repetition, separately for W0→W12 and W0→W24. Rows are observed response and columns model-estimated response. Diagonal cells are correct; upper-right cells falsely indicate response and lower-left cells miss an observed responder. Percentages are within each observed-response row, so the lower-right percentage is sensitivity and the upper-left percentage specificity. Observed response uses observed baseline/follow-up scores, whereas estimated response uses predicted baseline/follow-up scores. Counts are integers from one repetition, not the primary two-repetition average; the full metrics table retains the latter. The paired denominators are 85 and 67, with no excluded pair for invalid baseline in this displayed repetition. The two intervals can share patients. This assesses response classification, not alternative-treatment outcomes or continuous-score equivalence.
